title: Simplify Quickstart hero journey with progressive visuals
creator: Marco Alvarez
description: Refresh the Quickstart landing hero and leading steps to reduce cognitive load for new developer signups. Deliver a set of responsive hero variants, progressive diagrams that reveal routing and cost controls, and a compact step-by-step screenshot flow for the Quickstart docs. Focus on developer clarity (copy + code snippet prominence), fast visual load, and assets that can be reused across docs and the marketing site.
tasks: Audit existing hero variants and asset library (identify non-reusable PNGs)
Create 3 hero concepts: Code-first, Platform-diagram, Minimal sample-app walkthrough
Design progressive SVG diagrams that animate on scroll (Lottie fallback)
Update copy for first-time developer flow with PM (align with onboarding funnel)
Produce final hi-fi screens and export responsive breakpoints (desktop/tablet/mobile)
Coordinate with frontend for image/svg performance budget and lazy-loading strategy
Capture up-to-date product screenshots from staging (console-2025.10) and annotate steps
Run a 5-user usability check and collect heatmap/interactions for hero CTA
Prepare Figma package and handoff checklist for engineering; add tokens to design system
decisions: Single-column responsive hero on mobile to prioritize code snippet and CTA
Use SVG illustrations + small Lottie micro-interactions; serve GIF fallback under 100KB for low-capability clients
Show a progressive diagram that reveals routing -> model variant -> cost control on scroll rather than all at once
Keep primary CTA as 'Try Quickstart' (developer flow) and secondary as 'Read docs' (product flow)
Avoid heavy hero videos to maintain sub-200ms LCP target for the landing page
comments: 2025-09-12 Marco Alvarez: Kickoff meeting with PM (Priya) and Eng (Noah). Agreed scope: hero + 3 step screens + progressive diagram. Estimate 5pts.
2025-09-18 Lena Park: Initial wireframes posted to Figma. PM suggested emphasizing 'Try Quickstart' CTA over marketing copy for better conversion.
2025-09-22 Usability session: 5 dev participants. Key finding: participants looked for inline code snippet before using CTA; suggested we surface a minimal runnable snippet.
2025-09-26 Eng feedback (Noah): Need assets under 150KB for hero; prefer SVG-first and Lottie only for desktop; mobile should be static SVG.
2025-10-01 Design review: Andre from Brand requested color palette shift to improve contrast at small sizes. Updated token file accordingly.
2025-10-02 Lena Park: Hi-fi ready in Figma. Frontend PR opened and blocked pending exported assets and accessibility tests. See GH PR linked above.
